profile.headline: Biostatistics Research Software Engineer
profile.summary:
Clinical programmer using R for oncology research and development. 
Research software engineer building tools for biomarker statistical analysis. 
Experienced in genomic, epigenetic, transcriptomic, and proteomic data analysis.

positions.title: Research Software Engineer
positions.description: Oncology Data Strategy research software engineer, working to help patients live longer.

positions.title: Senior Statistical Program Analyst Project Lead
positions.description:
Developed data solutions with R Shiny, Markdown, AWS, BASH.
Integrated complex clinical data (SDTM and ADaM) for a wide range of indications.
Created interactive applications, data tables, databases, plots, heat maps, knowledge graphs for complex integrated datasets.
Mentored a group of data scientists in best programming practices.

positions.title: Senior Data Scientist
positions.description:
Analyzed phase I and II clinical trial data to help cancer patient treatment selection.
Developed custom research applications for data visualization. 
Managed software development and data curation teams.
Integrated NGS data processing pipelines to acquire knowledge.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
Designed research biosample database for Encyclopedia of DNA Elements (ENCODE). 
Wrangled data for analysis working group efforts to define functional aspects of the human genome.

positions.title: Bioinformaticist
positions.description:
Modeled cancer-specific and tissue-specific epigenetic data to learn oncogenic features. 
Managed data ingestion and controlled vocabulary for the UCSC Genome Browser (http://www.genome.ucsc.edu/), ENCODE project and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA).

positions.title: Human Embryonic Stem Cell Researcher (Advanced Cell Technology)
positions.description: Defined early progenitor cell line characteristics to accelerate human embryonic stem cell research.

positions.title: Transcriptome Researcher (Affymetrix)
positions.description: Discovered novel temporal transcriptional start sites (TSS) associated with early development.
